section_summary: This section records U.S. efforts to obtain economic intelligence from Japanese radio broadcasts monitored in China and the Soviet Union. Embassy telegrams summarize broadcasts about banking, currencies, agriculture, industry, transport and trade across Japanese-controlled Asia, while longer enclosures preserve the underlying translated reports. The section also includes requests for more frequent monitoring, notes on Japanese propaganda, and correspondence about obtaining a broadcast speech by Saburō Kurusu.

subfiles.title: Request for Chinese monitoring reports
subfiles.from: Department of State for Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: The Board requests daily summaries and copies of Chinese reports on Japanese broadcasts.
subfiles.summary: Requests immediate access to Chinese monitoring reports and daily economic summaries.

subfiles.title: Cable request concerning Chinese monitoring
subfiles.from: Document Security Section, Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.to: Board of Economic Warfare liaison officer, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Board submits the text of its monitoring request for transmission.
subfiles.summary: Supplies the cable sent to Chungking and bears William T. Stone’s approval.

subfiles.title: Economic broadcasts, July 29–August 6, section one
subfiles.about: The Embassy summarizes Chinese-monitored broadcasts on communications, banks and food supplies.
subfiles.summary: Reports new wireless links, bank openings and currency changes, plus Japanese claims about rice, sugar and fishing.

subfiles.title: Economic broadcasts, July 29–August 6, section two
subfiles.about: The Embassy continues its economic summary and asks whether the Board wants further reports.
subfiles.summary: Covers Singapore, North China infrastructure, occupation measures, Malayan food shortages, Borneo banking and military savings; notes the items originated as Domei dispatches.

subfiles.title: Treasury transmittal of telegram no. 960
subfiles.about: The State Department forwards Chungking’s first section of economic broadcast reporting.
subfiles.summary: Encloses telegram no. 960 on Japanese broadcasts of August 6–17.

subfiles.title: Treasury transmittal of telegram no. 960, section two
subfiles.about: The State Department forwards the second section of Chungking’s broadcast report.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the financial and economic portion of telegram no. 960.

subfiles.title: Economic broadcasts, August 6–17, section one
subfiles.about: The Embassy reports monitored broadcasts on banking, trade and food administration.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes Shanghai bank controls, liquidation of banks in the Philippines, resumed Hong Kong–Canton trade, and food and transport measures in Java.

subfiles.title: Economic broadcasts, August 6–17, section two
subfiles.about: The Embassy continues its summary of occupation economic policies.
subfiles.summary: Covers military yen, transport, a Tianjin blockade, rubber production, Philippine bank branches, North China prices and Japanese trade missions.

subfiles.title: Request for weekly broadcast reports
subfiles.from: Department of State for Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: The Board asks for weekly telegraphic reports on important economic broadcasts.
subfiles.summary: Specifies commodities, industry, shipping, transport, power and finance as reporting subjects.

subfiles.title: Cable request for weekly broadcast reports
subfiles.from: Document Security Section, Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.to: Board of Economic Warfare liaison officer, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Board submits its weekly-reporting cable for dispatch.
subfiles.summary: Repeats the reporting request and subject list; approved by William T. Stone.

subfiles.title: Chungking response on monitoring coverage
subfiles.about: The Embassy explains that its earlier telegrams covered the economic items available.
subfiles.summary: Refers the Board to telegrams nos. 899, 937 and 960.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Chungking response
subfiles.about: A paraphrase restates the Embassy’s answer about the Chinese monitoring service.
subfiles.summary: Says earlier telegrams reported the pertinent economic material and asks that the Board be informed.

subfiles.title: Economic broadcasts, August 18–26, section one
subfiles.about: The Embassy summarizes monitored broadcasts on development and production.
subfiles.summary: Covers an Asian development association, Philippine farming, Sumatra cotton, cargo junks, agricultural research and textile controls.

subfiles.title: Economic broadcasts, August 18–26, section two
subfiles.about: The Embassy continues its summary of Japanese economic measures.
subfiles.summary: Reports salt monopoly plans, Manchurian banking, fapi prohibitions, Shanghai banks, Philippine cotton, Mongolian exchange, rice imports and Japanese expenditures.

subfiles.title: Japanese broadcasts forwarded from Moscow
subfiles.about: The Embassy forwards Soviet-received broadcasts about Japanese savings and administrative plans.
subfiles.summary: Reports savings totals, a planned East Asian conference, and reorganization of Japanese ministries.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Moscow broadcast telegram no. 805
subfiles.about: A paraphrase repeats the September broadcast report from Thompson.
subfiles.summary: Restates Japanese savings, conference plans and government reorganization.

subfiles.title: Chungking despatch no. 610
subfiles.from: C. E. Gauss, American Embassy, Chungking
subfiles.about: The Embassy sends translated Chinese monitoring reports behind its earlier telegrams.
subfiles.summary: Gauss describes arrangements with three Chinese monitoring services and explains why economic reports were sent periodically rather than daily. The enclosed translations formed the basis of telegrams nos. 937, 960 and 1022.

subfiles.title: Translations of economic items in Japanese broadcasts
subfiles.to: Department of State and Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: A translated collection preserves detailed broadcasts on occupied Asian economies from late July through August 1942.
subfiles.summary: The enclosure expands the Embassy’s telegraphic summaries with reports on wireless links, banks, currencies, food production, resource extraction, transport, textile and cotton plans, and trade. It includes Japanese statements about occupation controls in China and Southeast Asia, named officials and institutions, and detailed figures for Japan’s fiscal year ending July 1942.

subfiles.title: Economic broadcasts, August 26–September 21, section one
subfiles.about: The Embassy summarizes broadcasts on bonds, banks, transport and coal.
subfiles.summary: Reports North China bonds, a Philippine development bank, fapi restrictions, a proposed bank, oil delivery, Singapore salvage and Jehol coal development.

subfiles.title: Economic broadcasts, August 26–September 21, section two
subfiles.about: The Embassy continues its summary of economic administration in occupied territories.
subfiles.summary: Covers Philippine cotton and factories, Singapore banking, Java matches, Hong Kong trade, Borneo navigation, Nanjing banking regulations and Indochinese barter.

subfiles.title: Japanese broadcasts forwarded from Moscow, October 9
subfiles.about: Soviet-monitored broadcasts report Manchurian factories and Japanese rice and wages.
subfiles.summary: Lists projected factories, harvest labor and possible wage increases.

subfiles.title: Radio broadcasts to Latin America
subfiles.about: A file note points to a letter about Japanese broadcasts to Latin America.
subfiles.summary: References Justice Department letter filed as 894.20210/206.

subfiles.title: Japanese broadcasts forwarded from Moscow, October 17
subfiles.about: Soviet-monitored broadcasts discuss savings, mines, cotton and prices.
subfiles.summary: Reports Japanese savings and war finance, Manchurian power and mercury, Philippine cotton planning, agricultural prices and rice.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Moscow broadcast telegram no. 339
subfiles.about: A paraphrase repeats Thompson’s report on economic broadcasts.
subfiles.summary: Restates reports on savings, mining, Philippine cotton, food procurement, inflation and rice.

subfiles.title: Economic broadcasts, September 7–October 19
subfiles.about: The Embassy summarizes 32 economic items from Chinese monitoring services.
subfiles.summary: The items cover buses, roads, savings, fapi withdrawal, an economic conference, public budgets, banks, shipping, crops, coal, railways and insurance across Japanese-controlled territories. Several concern occupation authorities’ control of trade, food and finance.

subfiles.title: Japanese broadcasts from Moscow, November 4
subfiles.about: Broadcasts describe Manchurian labor, agriculture and industry.
subfiles.summary: Reports a Korea–Manchukuo conference, compulsory labor plans, bank withdrawals, group farming, roadbuilding and blast furnaces.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Moscow broadcast telegram no. 430
subfiles.about: A paraphrase repeats the Manchurian and Japanese broadcast items.
subfiles.summary: Restates reports on labor, farming, banking, roads and steel production.

subfiles.title: Batavia broadcast reports
subfiles.about: A file note points to a despatch requesting feedback on reports of Japanese broadcasts.
subfiles.summary: References despatch no. 5, filed as 894.20200/7.

subfiles.title: Trend of Japanese radio propaganda
subfiles.about: A file note summarizes a despatch on Japanese propaganda themes.
subfiles.summary: Notes broadcasts portraying Japan as welcomed leader of occupied Asian peoples.

subfiles.title: Economic broadcasts, October 5–November 11
subfiles.about: The Embassy summarizes 24 economic items from Chinese-monitored broadcasts.
subfiles.summary: Reports food conservation, trade agencies, communications, tobacco, mining, harbor work, currency exchange and resource plans. Other items describe Hong Kong shipbuilding and agriculture, fapi restrictions, cotton planting and property placed under Japanese control.

subfiles.title: Economic broadcasts, November 16–21
subfiles.about: The Embassy summarizes an Asian economic conference and other broadcast reports.
subfiles.summary: Covers regional economic coordination, Japanese coin collection, banking, Burmese rice, Malayan railways, fapi exchange, price controls, food conservation and revised Japanese rice estimates.

subfiles.title: Kurusu broadcast speech
subfiles.about: The Embassy offers to translate a Chinese version of Kurusu’s broadcast speech.
subfiles.summary: Requests instructions if the Department wants a translation sent by pouch.

subfiles.title: Corrected copy of Kurusu speech telegram
subfiles.about: A corrected copy repeats the offer to translate Kurusu’s speech.
subfiles.summary: Offers a pouch translation if requested.

subfiles.title: Request for translation of Kurusu speech
subfiles.about: The Department asks for a translation of the version of Kurusu’s speech held in Chungking.
subfiles.summary: Says only an abridged English Domei account is available in Washington.

subfiles.title: Japanese broadcasts from Moscow, December 2
subfiles.about: Soviet-monitored broadcasts report colonization, coal, finance and banking.
subfiles.summary: Covers Korean settlement in Manchukuo, Shanxi coal, war loan stamps, shortages, a Sungari dam, state bonds and small-bank closures.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Moscow broadcast telegram no. 514
subfiles.about: A paraphrase repeats the December economic broadcast report.
subfiles.summary: Restates reports on banking, Korean settlement, loans, irrigation, shortages and coal.

subfiles.title: Follow-up request for Japanese broadcast data
subfiles.about: The Board asks about progress in obtaining Japanese broadcast data.
subfiles.summary: Requests a progress report on the earlier monitoring inquiry.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Soviet monitoring
subfiles.from: Charles E. Bohlen, Division of European Affairs
subfiles.about: A Board official asks for more frequent reports and a list of Japanese stations heard in the Soviet Union.
subfiles.summary: Records G. Chaput’s requests and Bohlen’s promise to contact the Moscow Embassy.

subfiles.title: Request for fuller Soviet monitoring reports
subfiles.about: The Department requests more broadcast material and technical information on Japanese stations.
subfiles.summary: Asks for more frequent reports and station wavelengths and schedules to check U.S. coverage.

subfiles.title: Chungking despatch no. 711
subfiles.from: C. E. Gauss, American Embassy, Chungking
subfiles.about: Gauss transmits further translations of Chinese-monitored economic broadcasts.
subfiles.summary: Notes fewer reports after the Central News Agency ended its monitoring service.

subfiles.title: Further translations of economic broadcasts
subfiles.to: Department of State and Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: The enclosure expands broadcast items summarized in telegram no. 1146.
subfiles.summary: The surviving pages cover North China bonds and coal, Philippine banking and cotton, occupation controls on factories, trade and finance, plus Singapore shipping and Java matches. The enclosure continues beyond page 358.
